purpose: Evidence cards for LLM-based scheduler selection. These are observations, not hard-coded routing rules.

cards.observation: At 256 threads, Linux default delivered 137.8 TPS while scx_lockcoop delivered 4692.7 TPS and reduced p95 latency from 5512.9 ms to 112.7 ms.
cards.interpretation: Concentrated lock contention with NUMA-sensitive handoff can benefit from per-lock Lock Nest placement.
risks: Check fairness and zero-progress threads before committing a strong affinity policy.

cards.observation: At 256 threads, Linux default delivered 1899.7 TPS, scx_lockboost delivered 6007.2 TPS, scx_simple delivered 5773.4 TPS, and scx_lockcoop delivered 5102.1 TPS.
cards.interpretation: Owner progress and generic sched_ext behavior can dominate strong lock affinity for some database engines.
risks: Do not assume all OLTP workloads prefer scx_lockcoop.

cards.observation: At 256 clients, Linux default delivered 46854.5 TPS, scx_simple delivered 54132.8 TPS, scx_lockboost delivered 52414.0 TPS, and scx_lockcoop delivered 52406.2 TPS.
cards.interpretation: Some database workloads show modest gains and may not justify strong lock-specific intervention.
risks: Avoid overfitting the paper story to MariaDB.

cards.observation: In readwhilewriting at 128 threads, Linux default delivered about 2.76M ops/s while scx_lockcoop delivered about 0.62M ops/s. In readrandomwriterandom at 128 threads, scx_lockcoop was about 0.34x of default.
cards.interpretation: Many short-held locks and diverse lock addresses can make strong Lock Nest placement harmful.
risks: The agent must explicitly guard against affinity-induced parallelism collapse.

cards.observation: In updaterandom, scx_lockboost and scx_cfl improved throughput over Linux default in multiple configurations.
cards.interpretation: For write-heavy KV workloads, owner progress or lock occupation fairness may be safer than per-lock affinity.
risks: Validate p999 latency because throughput gains can hide tail regressions.

cards.observation: At 256 threads cs0, Linux default delivered 18.9K ops/s, scx_lockcoop delivered 263.9K ops/s, and scx_cfl delivered 334.7K ops/s with Jain fairness near 1.
cards.interpretation: Synchronous futex handoff chains can benefit from fairness-aware lock occupation control.
risks: Do not extrapolate futex ring behavior to all mutex workloads.

cards.observation: eBPF lock-monitor can introduce small timing perturbations on futex and wakeup paths; in extreme synchronized contention this may reduce useless wakeup, failed reacquire, and sleep cycles.
cards.interpretation: Micro-jitter is a monitor-layer phenomenon and a possible controlled policy only for high synchronized recontention.
risks: Jitter is not a default optimization. It can be pure overhead outside short critical-section synchronized contention.
